subject: literature
passage: Mrs. Dorrance had let her second-floor room to young men from the counting-houses for eleven years, and she had formed, in that time, a theory of them which Mr. Pell did nothing to disturb. He was punctual with his rent, silent on the stairs, and so entirely without conversation that she had concluded, by October, that he had no thoughts at all. It was therefore with some astonishment that she found him, one evening in January, kneeling at the grate in her own parlor, explaining to her youngest, who had been crying over his arithmetic, that there was nothing in the world so obliging as a number if one only asked it civilly. She stood in the doorway for a full minute before either of them noticed her, and she went back to the kitchen revising, with some reluctance, a theory of eleven years' standing.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To show how an unexpected scene leads a character to reconsider a settled judgment about another person
choices.B: To contrast the kindness of a lodger with the coldness of the landlady who misjudged him
choices.C: To describe the routine a landlady follows in managing the young men who rent her rooms
choices.D: To suggest that quiet people are generally more intelligent than talkative ones

explanation.why: The text establishes Mrs. Dorrance's long-held "theory" of her lodgers and her conclusion that Mr. Pell "had no thoughts at all." The January scene, in which he patiently helps her child, contradicts that theory, and the final sentence shows her "revising, with some reluctance," a judgment of eleven years. The purpose is to show a settled opinion being overturned by an unexpected scene.
explanation.A: Correct. Her theory, the surprising sight of Mr. Pell at the grate, and her reluctant revision of "a theory of eleven years' standing."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Mrs. Dorrance is not portrayed as cold; her "reluctance" is gently comic, and the text treats her misjudgment with humor rather than blame.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Her eleven years of lodgers are background for her theory; the text is about that theory being upset.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text concerns one lodger and one landlady and makes no general claim about quiet people.
